system.name: Eta Carinae
system.description: A colossal luminous blue variable 7,500 light-years away in the Carina Nebula. The primary star is one of the most massive and luminous known, and the system famously produced the Great Eruption of 1843 — temporarily making it the second-brightest star in the sky.

etacarinae.name: Eta Carinae A
etacarinae.description: A luminous blue variable of roughly 150 solar masses — one of the most massive and luminous stars known. It is surrounded by the Homunculus Nebula, a bipolar cloud of gas ejected during the Great Eruption of 1843, when the star temporarily became the second-brightest in the sky without exploding.
etacarinae.funFact: During the Great Eruption of 1843, Eta Carinae released as much energy in 10 years as the Sun emits in 10 million years — yet it survived. It is one of the best candidates for the next hypernova in our galaxy.

etacarinaeb.name: Eta Carinae B
etacarinaeb.description: A massive companion star — likely an O supergiant or Wolf-Rayet star of roughly 30 solar masses — on a highly eccentric 5.54-year orbit. At closest approach it plunges through Eta Carinae A's dense stellar wind, producing dramatic X-ray flares observable from Earth.
etacarinaeb.funFact: At periastron Eta Carinae B dives so deep into the primary's wind that it triggers a predictable X-ray minimum visible from Earth every 5.54 years — a clockwork heartbeat from 7,500 light-years away.
